[engine] Before quoting a probe as evidence about what a CONSUMER received, establish when the probe runs relative to the write it is measuring; a host-side read taken during graph encoding of a device-written tensor measures the buffer's pre-write occupant, so it tracks WHO writes the buffer, not whether the value is correct.

<!-- lesson_id: eng-mh-0008 | class: measurement-hygiene | superseded_by: - -->

**class**: `measurement-hygiene`

## 為什麼（because）

CGC-MMID-ASSERT reads ((int32_t *) op->src[2]->data)[i] inside the mul_mat_id ENCODE path of ggml-metal-ops.cpp. While src[2] was the host-written leaf that read was meaningful (id_oob=0/240); once src[2] became the device-computed gather output the same probe reported id_oob=16/16 at layer 1 and a cumulative 202000, with first=1063585220 (0x3F65.. = F32 0.90) and 1058604036 (0x3F19.. = F32 0.60) -- i.e. router probabilities, the previous occupant of a reused buffer. The same arm under the non-segmented dispatcher read id_oob=0/288. Both readings produced readable French, so neither number tracked the answer. The baseline's 0 is what makes this dangerous: it looks like 'the baseline is clean' and invites the reading 'S1 corrupts the ids'. The sound provenance fields (ids_name, ids_op, ids_data) were in the same log line all along, and they already answer the only question this probe can actually answer: host-written vs device-written.
